newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes depressed, Minas discounts deepens.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes depressed, Minas discounts deepens.

text.p: Asian crudes weakened as the continued absence of China closed off the main outlet for heavy sweet grades such as Minas, traders said.
A Japanese refiner bought up to 300,000 barrels of June Minas Friday at ICP -15/20 cents per barrel from two sellers.
Details on the sellers were sketchy, although they were both heard to be shoshas.
Only Duri crude was holding its strength and traders expected demand from fuel oil blenders to maintain the crude's price around ICP +30 for July.
June Duri was sold out, with last trades done at ICP +30.
Award details of a Bach Ho sales tender by Vietnam, which closed on Wednesday, could not be confirmed, although the level was heard to be OSP +64.
With Bach Ho's OSP at Minas APPI +80, the level of the award was considered by some traders to be extremely high.
But others considered the level comparative to the Minas price, as the Minas APPI is much lower than the Minas ICP.
Traders said the award was likely to have been to a shosha.
In the Middle East market, prices steadied in thin trading.
Traders were uncertain about the direction of the Oman market, following the last trades at MPM -23/24 two days ago.
Rumours circulated of new Oman deals done around MPM -25, or lower, but they could not be confirmed.
There was healthy demand for July Masila from China, which could spill over into the Oman market, providing a floor to Oman prices, traders said.

On the light Middle East crudes, negotiations were heard going on between a Euro major and a U.S. major for the last July Umm Shaif cargo, but there was no trade concluded late in the day. Traders said one and a half Murban cargoes were also on offer for July. --Azlin Ahmad, Singapore (+65 870 3199)
